# Ten conditional hypotheses for NAS-Bench-201 edits

Each hypothesis borrows a pattern from another empirical field and maps it onto how signals flow through the cell. In the flaw step I dropped two analogies:

- **Pure economic diminishing returns on the serial conv chain (edge 0 given edge 2 = conv3x3).** Whether an upstream edge matters at all depends on its downstream consumers being live. That effect probably outweighs saturation.
- **"Fitter backgrounds gain less" applied to whole-cell fitness.** The NB201 accuracy ceiling is too loose to make this predictive edge by edge.

I kept analogies where a structural reason in the cell makes them likely to hold.

| # | Edit | Condition | Direction | Analogy → mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | e0 → nor_conv_3x3 | e0 = nor_conv_1x1 | lower | Diminishing returns. Upgrading an existing conv gains less than replacing none, skip or pool. |
| 2 | e0 → nor_conv_3x3 | e4 = none | lower | Epistasis by masking. Node 1 then reaches the output only through e2, so e0 matters less. |
| 3 | e3 → skip_connect | e5 = nor_conv_3x3 | higher | Redundancy and bypass. A residual shortcut is worth most when a deep conv path feeds the output. |
| 4 | e3 → nor_conv_3x3 | e3 = skip_connect | lower | Background-dependent sign. Top cells keep e3 as skip, so replacing skip gains less, or loses, compared with replacing none or pool. |
| 5 | e5 → avg_pool_3x3 | e4 = nor_conv_3x3 | higher | Parallel compensation. A strong parallel conv into node 3 cushions the loss of conv on e5. |
| 6 | e4 → skip_connect | e3 = skip_connect | lower | Redundancy without benefit. A second unnormalized identity input skews the activation scale at node 3. |
| 7 | e4 → skip_connect | e4 = none | higher | Gain of function vs loss of function. Adding a new input helps, while replacing a conv with skip hurts. |
| 8 | e5 → none | e3 = none | lower | Synthetic lethality. Removing a second input to the output can leave it nearly dead. |
| 9 | e1 → nor_conv_3x3 | e5 = none | lower | Masking. Node 2 then reaches the output only through nothing, so e1 is nearly irrelevant. |
| 10 | e2 → nor_conv_3x3 | e0 = none | lower | Upstream null. A conv on an all-zero input from node 1 adds no signal. |

The most counter-intuitive predictions are #4, #6 and #7. In these, skip_connect's average weakness or the "conv is always better" prior should give the wrong answer, depending on the background.
